svg.title: For a plane source il, form the potential Ab = δib∂lgt−δlb∂igt, and take its exterior derivative. It satisfies the Bianchi identity by commutation of derivatives, while its divergence is δlb∂iρt −δib∂lρt. The divergence of its bilinear stress with the source-free field f is therefore the contraction of this expression with f; the terms from the symmetric derivative of v cancel by tracelessness and the other terms cancel by skew symmetry. Integration by parts against χ transfers the source derivatives to the smooth compact test made from χ, v, f. The preceding approximate-identity limit evaluates their difference at x, giving −δvfil(x). On the shell the regulated exterior derivative converges smoothly to the pulse, since that compact shell avoids x. Its flux thus converges to the left side of (FS2). This proves the plane-source case with the stated sign.
